To strongly differentiate the models, we need to introduce conditions that selectively penalize or reward specific mechanistic features. By adding a significant initial product concentration (P = 0.5), we can isolate models that feature product inhibition or product-induced deactivation (M5, M12, M17). Simultaneously, lowering the catalyst concentration by an order of magnitude (to 0.01) will drastically alter the relative rates of bimolecular catalyst interactions (such as dimerization in M2, M3, or second-order deactivation in M13, M19) compared to unimolecular pathways. Finally, reducing the initial substrate concentration (to 0.5) will shift the steady-state distribution of free catalyst versus the catalyst-substrate complex, providing leverage to distinguish substrate-induced deactivation (M11, M16) and higher-order substrate binding (M7). This multi-pronged perturbation is designed to pull apart the tightly clustered NLL values by testing dependencies on all three species simultaneously.
</hypothesis>
